334582.title: Haralambis' equality conjecture for three-element distance sets
334582.literal_statement:
Let $D$ be a three-element set of non-negative integers. Let $\kappa(D)$ be the supremum, over real $t$, of the smallest distance from $td$ to an integer as $d$ ranges over $D$, and let $\mu(D)$ be the supremum of the densities of sequences whose pairwise differences do not lie in $D$.

**Haralambis' equality conjecture.** Every three-element $D$-set satisfies

$$
\kappa(D)=\mu(D).
$$

The conjecture is presented in the conclusion as a particularly interesting problem because exact computation of $\mu(D)$ is difficult in general. The supplied text gives no resolution status.

334645.title: Davila–Kenter's lower-bound conjecture for the zero forcing number
334645.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with girth $g\ge 3$ and minimum degree $\delta\ge 2$. Its zero forcing number $Z(G)$ is the minimum cardinality of a zero forcing set, where a zero forcing set is a set of initially black vertices from which the color-change rule eventually colors every vertex black.

**Davila–Kenter's conjecture.**

$$
Z(G) \ge \delta + (\delta - 2)(g - 3).
$$

This conjecture gives a readily computable lower bound for the zero forcing number, a graph invariant introduced in connection with minimum-rank problems for matrices associated with graphs. The source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

334675.title: Aharoni–Zerbib's generalization of Tuza's conjecture
334675.literal_statement:

**Aharoni–Zerbib's generalization of Tuza's conjecture.** Every $3$-uniform hypergraph satisfies

$$
\tau^{(2)}(H)\leq 2\nu^{(2)}(H).
$$

This extends the triangle-hypergraph formulation of Tuza's conjecture to all $3$-uniform hypergraphs. The source gives no resolution status.

334830.title: Uniform condition-number conjecture for the trace Schur complement
334830.literal_statement:
Let $\lambda_{\min}(s,h)$ and $\lambda_{\max}(s,h)$ be respectively the smallest and largest generalized eigenvalues of the trace Schur-complement matrix relative to the fractional norm matrix ${\mathsf{H}}_s$, with $s<0$. Define the condition number by

$$
\kappa(s,h)=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(s,h)}{\lambda_{\min}(s,h)}.
$$

**Uniform condition-number conjecture.** There exist $s<0$ and a constant $C$ such that

$$
\kappa(s,h)\leq C\qquad\forall h>0.
$$

This weaker requirement asks only for a mesh-independent condition number, rather than uniform lower and upper spectral-equivalence bounds; the source presents it as an additional computational criterion.

334858.title: Bump-Friedberg generating-function identity for covering groups
334858.literal_statement:
Let $(\widetilde{\operatorname{GL}}_r^{(n)},\widetilde{\operatorname{GL}}_R^{(n)})$ be a fundamental pair with $n\mid(\mathbf{p}\cdot n_\alpha)$. Let $\Theta(\widetilde{\operatorname{GL}}_R^{(n)},\chi)$ be the distinguished theta representation whose associated character satisfies $\nu_R=\mathbf{1}$, and let $\mathcal{W}^{\operatorname{GL}_R}_{\mathcal{O}_0}$ be its unique Whittaker model. Let $\widetilde{\Delta}_s$ be the anti-genuine, $K_r$-biinvariant function on $\widetilde{\operatorname{GL}}_r^{(n)}$ specified by the stated torus support and value. **Bump-Friedberg identity.** For every $\widetilde{g}\in\widetilde{\operatorname{GL}}_r^{(n)}$,

$$
\int_{U_r}\widetilde{\Delta}_{n_\alpha s-\frac{R-1}{2}}(u\widetilde{g})\psi(u)\,du=|\det(\widetilde{g})|^{s-\frac{R-r}{2}}\overline{\mathcal{W}^{\operatorname{GL}_R}_{\mathcal{O}_0}}(\phi(\widetilde{g})).
$$

This identity is presented in the supplied text as a consequence of the generating-function approach of Bump and Friedberg to the Bump-Hoffstein conjecture; no resolution evidence is supplied.

334880.title: Threshold conjecture for universality in bounded-degree graphs

$$
p\sim\left(n^{-1}\log^{1/\Delta}n\right)^{\frac{2}{\Delta+1}}.
$$
 This is the threshold for the appearance of $K_{\Delta+1}$-factors; the conjecture asserts that the threshold for one such factor is also the threshold for the simultaneous appearance of every graph in $\mathcal{H}(n,\Delta)$.

334900.literal_statement:

334944.title: Milans–Stolee–West conjecture on unbounded track number of line graphs
334944.literal_statement:

$$
\chi(G_n) \mathrel{\longrightarrow} \infty,

then

$$
\tau(L(G_n)) \mathrel{\longrightarrow} \infty.

334963.title: Conjecture on the circular separation dimension of planar graphs
334963.literal_statement:

$$
\pi^\circ(G)\leq 2.
$$

335009.title: Conjecture on transfers of test functions
335009.literal_statement:
Let $E \geq F' \geq F$ be a tower of number fields, let $S$ be a finite set of places of $F$ containing the infinite places, and let $S'$ and $S_0$ be the places of $F'$ and $E$ above $S$. Let $\Pi$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_E)$, and suppose $\Pi^{\sigma}\cong\Pi$ for every $\sigma\in\mathrm{Gal}(E/F)$. A transfer is a triple of compactly supported smooth functions $f_{S_0}$, $h_{S'}$, and $\Phi_S$ satisfying the trace identity of Definition of the paper for every irreducible generic unitary representation $\pi_S$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F_S)$; a function is of positive type in the sense used there. **Transfer conjecture.** There exist $f_{S_0}\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathrm{GL}_n(E_{S_0}))$ and $h_{S'}\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathrm{GL}_n(F'_{S'}))$ admitting a transfer $\Phi_S\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathrm{GL}_n(F_S))$ of positive type such that the transfer identity holds for every irreducible generic unitary representation $\pi_S$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F_S)$ and

$$
\mathrm{tr}(\Pi_{S_0})(f_{S_0})\neq 0.
$$

The conjecture asserts that sufficiently many transfers can detect every Galois-invariant cuspidal representation; the paper notes that it is known in some special settings, including $n=2$ and cyclic extensions of prime degree, but remains open in general.

335070.title: The maximum principle conjecture for the Riesz transform
335070.literal_statement:
Let $\mu$ be a nonnegative finite Borel measure with compact support and continuous density with respect to the Lebesgue measure in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $0<s<d$. The $s$-Riesz transform (potential) of $\mu$ is

$$
R^s\mu(x)=\int\frac{y-x}{|y-x|^{s+1}}\,d\mu(y).
$$

**Maximum principle conjecture.** There is a constant $C=C(d,s)$ such that

$$
\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}|R^s\mu(x)|\le C\sup_{x\in\operatorname{supp}\mu}|R^s\mu(x)|.
$$

This relation was known for $d-1\le s<d$ and is proved in the paper for $0<s<1$ and for radial measures, while it remains open in the general case. The conjecture is stated for nonnegative measures; it is false for non-positive measures.

335136.title: The hemisphere volume conjecture for metric balls
335136.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold of dimension $n$, let $B(p,R)$ be a metric ball, and let $inj(M)$ denote the injectivity radius. A hemisphere of intrinsic radius $R$ is a ball of radius $R$ in the sphere of constant curvature $(\frac{\pi}{2R})^2$. Let $\alpha(n)$ denote the volume of the unit $n$-sphere. **Hemisphere volume conjecture.** If

$$
R \leq \frac{1}{2}inj(M),
$$

then

$$
Vol(B(p,R))\geq \frac{\alpha(n)}{2}\left(\frac{2R}{\pi}\right)^n.
$$

Equality holds if and only if $B(p,R)$ is isometric to a hemisphere of intrinsic radius $R$. Hemispheres are conjectured to have the smallest volume among metric balls of fixed dimension and radius; nonsharp lower bounds are known in all dimensions, but the sharp conjecture remains open even in dimension two.

335208.title: Maximum-gap sampling conjecture for shift-invariant spline spaces
335208.literal_statement:
Let $Q_m$ denote the spline generator and let $V(Q_m)$ be the shift-invariant spline space it generates. A sequence $\\{x_i:i\in\mathbb{Z}\\}$ is **separated** if its distinct points have a positive minimum separation. **Maximum-gap sampling conjecture.** If $\\{x_i:i\in\mathbb{Z}\\}$ is a separated set with

$$
\sup\limits_{i}(x_{i+\nu}-x_i)<\nu,
$$

then $\\{x_i:i\in\mathbb{Z}\\}$ is a stable set of sampling for $V(Q_m)$. This extends the known case $\nu=1$ and is motivated by the sharp maximum-gap results for entire functions of exponential type $\pi$ and the shift-invariant space generated by the Meyer scaling function; the corresponding assertion for general $\nu\geq 1$ remains open.

335209.title: Maximum-gap derivative sampling conjecture for shift-invariant spaces
335209.literal_statement:
Let $V(\phi)$ be a shift-invariant space, let $k$ and $\nu$ be positive integers, and let $\\{x_i:i\in\mathbb{Z}\\}$ be a separated set. For a function $f$, consider the nonuniform samples of its derivatives $f^{(j)}(x_i)$ for $j=0,\dots,k-1$. **Maximum-gap derivative sampling conjecture.** If

$$
\sup\limits_{i}(x_{i+\nu}-x_i)<k\nu,
$$

then every function $f\in V(\phi)$ can be reconstructed stably from its nonuniform sample values $\\{f^{(j)}(x_i):j=0,\dots,k-1, i\in\mathbb{Z}\\}$. The statement generalizes the preceding maximum-gap sampling conjecture to simultaneous derivative sampling, but no resolution is given in the source.

335224.title: Fomin–Zelevinsky's C-matrix conjecture for cluster algebras
335224.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal A_{t_0}$ be the cluster algebra with principal coefficients at $\Sigma_{t_0}$, and let

$$
\Sigma_t=(X_t,\widetilde B_t)
$$

be a seed of $\mathcal A_{t_0}$ obtained from $\Sigma_{t_0}$ by iterated mutations. Write

$$
\widetilde B_t=\begin{pmatrix}B_t\\C_t\end{pmatrix},
$$

where $C_t$ is the lower part, called the **C-matrix**. **Fomin–Zelevinsky's C-matrix conjecture.** The seed $\Sigma_t$ is uniquely determined by $C_t$. This conjecture concerns the extent to which coefficient data determine seeds in cluster algebras; in the setting of the paper, the stated result is proved using positivity of cluster variables and sign-coherence of $c$-vectors, while related weaker conclusions are discussed for the sign-skew-symmetric case.

335230.title: The complete multipartite fractional-defect conjecture
335230.literal_statement:
For positive integers $m$, $a$, and $k$, let $K^{(m)}_a$ be the complete $m$-partite graph with $a$ vertices in each partite set. Let $D(G,k)$ denote the minimum defect in a fractional $k$-coloring of $G$. **Complete multipartite fractional-defect conjecture.** The minimum defect in a $k$-coloring of $K^{(m)}_a$ is

$$
\left(\left\lceil \frac{m}{k}\right\rceil-1\right)a.
$$

When $m$ is a multiple of $k$, this value is known to be optimal. The conjecture concerns the remaining values of $m$ and predicts that the natural upper bound remains exact.

335257.title: Kahn's bounded-degree spanning tree conjecture
335257.literal_statement:
Fix $\Delta$, and let $T=(T_n)$ be a fixed sequence of trees on $n$ vertices satisfying $\Delta(T)\le \Delta$. Write $G(n,p)$ for the binomial random graph.

**Kahn's conjecture.** There is a constant $C$ such that, if $p\ge C\log n/n$, then $G(n,p)$ almost surely contains $T$.

This conjecture asserts that the Hamilton-path threshold extends to every fixed sequence of spanning trees with bounded maximum degree. 335258.title: The bounded-degree spanning graph threshold conjecture
335258.literal_statement:
Fix a constant $\Delta$, and let $H=(H_n)$ be a sequence of graphs with maximum degree $\Delta(H)\le \Delta$ and at most $n$ vertices, $v(H)\le n$.

**Bounded-degree spanning graph threshold conjecture.** The random graph $G(n,p)$ almost surely contains $H$ whenever

$$
p\cdot\frac{n^{2/(\Delta+1)}}{(\log n)^{1/\binom{\Delta+1}{2}}}\to\infty.
$$

Equivalently, the conjectured threshold is the threshold for a $K_{\Delta+1}$-factor. The source says this optimum is widely believed and gives no resolution.

335259.title: Resilience conjecture for universality of bounded-degree spanning trees
335259.literal_statement:
Fix $\Delta\ge 2$ and $\gamma>0$. Let $\mathcal{T}(n,\Delta)$ denote the family of spanning trees on $n$ vertices with maximum degree at most $\Delta$. The **local resilience** of a graph with respect to a property is the largest number of incident edges that may be deleted at every vertex while the property is retained.

**Bounded-degree tree universality resilience conjecture.** The conclusion of the cited resilience theorem—that the local resilience of $G(n,p)$ with respect to being universal for $\mathcal{T}(n,\Delta)$ is almost surely at least $\frac12-\gamma$—holds for $p\ge C\log n/n$.

The source says this probability is conjectured to be optimal up to constants, while the stated theorem only establishes the conclusion for $p\ge C(\log n/n)^{1/3}$.

335303.title: The spherical-twist conjecture for generic monodromy around discriminants
335303.literal_statement:
Let a component of the discriminant in the parameter space of a GLSM be given, and let the associated Higgs GLSM determine a category of D-branes, denoted by $\mathsf{A}$. A spherical twist is the autoequivalence associated with a spherical functor from $\mathsf{A}$ to the D-brane category of the original theory.

**Generic monodromy conjecture.** The generic monodromy around the component of the discriminant is given by a spherical twist, where $\mathsf{A}$ is the category of D-branes in the associated Higgs GLSM.

335392.literal_statement:

335442.title: Covert–Koh–Pham even-dimensional k-resultant modulus conjecture
335442.literal_statement:
Let $E_1,\ldots,E_k\subset\mathbb F_q^d$, with $k\geq 2$, and define

$$
\Delta_k(E_1,\ldots,E_k)=\left\{\left\|{\bf x}^1+\cdots+{\bf x}^k\right\|\in\mathbb F_q:{\bf x}^j\in E_j,\ j=1,\ldots,k\right\}.
$$

Let $\gamma_k$ be the smallest exponent such that $\prod_{j=1}^k|E_j|\geq Cq^{\gamma_k}$ implies $|\Delta_k(E_1,\ldots,E_k)|\geq cq$. **Covert–Koh–Pham conjecture.** If $d\geq 2$ is even and $k\geq 2$, then

$$
\gamma_k=\frac{kd}{2}.
$$

The exponent is motivated by the example $q=p^2$ with $E_j=\mathbb F_p^d$, which has product size $q^{kd/2}$ but a generalized resultant modulus set of size only $\sqrt q$. The problem remains open in the stated even-dimensional generality.
